questions.label: Q.1(a)
questions.stem: How is problem defined in the opinion of a common man?
questions.context: It is said that there is no man in this world who does not have a problem. To a common man, a problem can be anything that disturbs his equilibrium because it prevents him from achieving something that he wants. It can also be anything that poses a difficulty to him or compounds a situation for him. It means that we are not free from problems. Since we do not live in a utopian world where everything is hunky dory we encounter many problems. If a student cannot find his pencil he has a problem. If the Prime Minister of the country can't find a solution to overcome the pandemic he has a problem. If the roof of a house is damaged by hailstones, a family has a problem. If somebody talks ill of us in our absence, we have a problem. If we are not allowed to go somewhere by our parents we have a problem. If we harm an innocent person by mistake we have a problem. Problems vary from person to person in terms of their complexity and seriousness. A situation that could be seen by a person as a problem may not be seen in the same way by some other person. A problem may affect an individual, a family, a community, a nation or the entire world. We create problems for ourselves in many ways. Many problems will disappear from our life when we manage our time well, respect our elders, show kindness to others and love the nature. When we manage our time well, we are able to execute many tasks we had planned for ourselves. It makes us feel a sense of achievement. When we are absorbed in our work, our mind ceases to become a devil's workshop. When we listen to our parents, we become good human beings. When we show kindness to others, we become better human beings. When we take care of the nature, natural calamities do not take birth. There are some people in this world who love to have those situations which many would call problems. These situations are opportunities for them to test themselves. They strongly believe that these opportunities teach them many lessons of life and eventually help them become better versions of themselves
questions.subject: English

questions.label: Q.2(a)
questions.stem: What do the weavers weave in the early morning?
questions.context:
Indian Weavers
Weavers, weaving at break of day,
Why do you weave a garment so gay?
Blue as the wing of a bluebird wild,
We weave the robes of a new- born child.
Weavers, weaving at fall of night,
Why do weave garment so bright?
Like the plumes of a peacock, purple or green,
We weave the marriage veils of a queen
Weavers, weaving solemn and still,
What do you weave in moonlight chill?
White as a feather and white as a cloud,
We weave a dead man's funeral shroud.

questions.label: Q.4
questions.stem:
Read the following passage and draft a precis.
There are different kinds of students in a school. They are usually categorised as good, naughty and weak. Good students are characterised by intelligence, obedience, punctuality and modesty. Naughty students are quite problematic. They may be intelligent but they disturb the class by causing distraction both for the teachers as well as the taught. They may pick up a quarrel with anybody anytime. They may also steal a pen, a book or anything from the other students. Weak students are those who don't do well in their exams. There are many factors that could make a student weak. He is not familiar with his lessons because he cannot understand what the teachers are teaching in the class. It may be attributed to lack of good foundation, lack of confidence, lack of motivation, or lack of proper guidance. Teachers and parents need to work as a team to find out the cause of a student's weakness. They must motivate him, clarify his doubts and help set realistic goals for himself.

Fill in the blanks by choosing the appropriate verb.
(a) A number of people______ going to attend the function. (is/are)
(b) Dal and rice ______my favourite dish. (is/are)
(c) Most of the sugar ______ been sold. (has/have)
(d) Half of his income______ spent on construction of his house. (was/were)
(e) The police ______ trying to catch the thief.(is/are)
(f) Neither Rohan nor the two students ______coming today.(is/are)
(g) One of the boys ______to watch horror movies.(like/likes)
(h) If I ______the prime minister, I would help the poor. (was/ were)
(i) Anil and Arun ______ playing in the park. (is/are)
(j) Aman as well as his friends ______ coming over for a party.(is/are)
